_comment: The shortlist. A technology is a candidate only when one of its use_when signals matches something concrete in the request; one avoid_when hit usually caps fit at Low. Read the card before saying anything beyond one_line. ecosystem-map.md covers projects without a card.

technologies.name: Ruflo
technologies.one_line: Add-on for Claude Code and Codex: multi-agent runs, shared memory, workflows and model-routing hints, as plugins or a full environment.
use_when: several agents must share searchable memory across runs or weeks
many agents change code in parallel and collide, needing worktree isolation and a shared decision record
per-step model routing or cost tracking at volume matters and would otherwise be hand-built
two or more of those needs at once, so assembling them from native Claude Code pieces is the bigger job
the user already runs Ruflo and one more Ruflo plugin fixes a current pain
the user explicitly wants to learn agent orchestration in a sandbox
avoid_when: parallelism or repetition is the only need: Claude Code's built-in subagents and a skill cover it
one agent can finish the task in one sitting
every step depends on the previous step's output
the product is a web app whose runtime isn't a coding assistant
the team needs a minimal, audited Claude Code configuration
nobody will track near-daily releases

technologies.name: RuVector
technologies.one_line: Embedded vector store in Rust with Node, browser and Postgres options: search by meaning locally, no server.
use_when: semantic search must run locally, offline, in the browser or at the edge
data must not leave the user's machine and an embedded store beats running a server
a Node.js or Rust project wants agent memory with a ready-made CLI and MCP server
vector and graph search are both needed in one embedded library
avoid_when: Postgres with pgvector already works for them
the stack is Python
they need stable semver, replication or incremental backups
the dataset is small (thousands of items)
queries rely on selective metadata filters

technologies.name: AgentDB
technologies.one_line: TypeScript library and MCP server that stores an agent's past tasks, outcomes and skills in a local file, searchable by meaning.
use_when: the agent must improve across sessions from recorded outcomes, and a real feedback signal exists
the user already runs Ruflo or agentic-flow, whose memory uses it
a JavaScript or TypeScript prototype wants episode and skill memory as MCP tools today
avoid_when: memory just means app data, which belongs in a normal table
there's no feedback signal or too little repetition to learn from
production or client work that needs stable releases
the data already lives in Postgres or SQLite
the stack isn't JavaScript or TypeScript

technologies.name: RVF
technologies.one_line: A single file that carries an agent's vectors, index, metadata and a tamper-evident history between programs.
technologies.status: research-draft spec, all 0.x, open data-fidelity bugs
use_when: agent memory has to move between machines, tools or customers as one file
a signed, tamper-evident history of what an agent knew is a stated requirement
they use AgentDB or Ruflo memory and need to understand or move the .rvf files
research or experimentation with the format itself, in a sandbox
avoid_when: anything production-critical
other tools need to read the data
portable just means exportable
encryption is the requirement

technologies.name: MetaHarness
technologies.one_line: Generates a stand-alone, publishable agent package (prompts, skills, MCP stub, host config) for a repo.
use_when: an agent setup has to be shipped to a client, team or the public as a versioned package
several repos each need a consistent, repo-specific agent configuration
the user wants to leave a full Ruflo project for something smaller they own
they want to preview a harness for their repo in a browser with nothing installed
avoid_when: one developer, one repo, nothing to distribute
they want a chatbot, a no-code platform, a hosted agent or fine-tuning
stability matters more than features

technologies.name: RuView
technologies.one_line: Camera-free presence, activity and pose sensing from WiFi signals, using inexpensive boards. Research-grade.
use_when: the project senses people or spaces and cameras aren't acceptable
the user is comfortable with hardware and research-grade accuracy
a lab, hobby or proof-of-concept sensing build
avoid_when: medical, safety-critical or legally sensitive use
the need is ordinary software: apps, agents, search, memory
a standard presence sensor would do

technologies.name: SPARC
technologies.one_line: Five gated phases for building with agents: Specification, Pseudocode, Architecture, Refinement, Completion.
use_when: features are big enough that a written spec and design step pay off
the agent keeps building the wrong thing and needs gates that force a plan first
they already run Ruflo and want the method inside it
avoid_when: small changes and bug fixes
the team already has a planning habit that works
they'd only adopt it through a heavy tool

technologies.name: agentic-flow
technologies.one_line: Toolkit for agent workflows and per-task model or provider switching on Claude Code and the Agent SDK; Ruflo builds on it.
use_when: a developer builds agent workflows in code and wants model or provider switching ready-made
they need a piece of Ruflo's underlying layer without the full environment
avoid_when: a beginner wants multi-agent work inside Claude Code
one model and one provider are fine
the dependency tree must be free of alphas

technologies.name: RuvNet Brain
technologies.one_line: Third-party Claude Code plugin by Stuart Kerr: source-level search over rUv projects, plus hooks that advocate rUv capabilities every session.
use_when: the user has decided to build on the rUv stack in Claude Code and wants grounded answers all day
they want Claude blocked from asserting rUv capabilities without checking source
they've graduated past ruv lite and want an advocate for the stack
avoid_when: they're still deciding whether to use rUv at all
they don't want hooks injecting text or gating writes in every session
they need a predictable, minimal Claude Code setup for a team
